_meta.name: ID Registry
_meta.purpose: Canonical registry of all prefixed IDs in the spec system. Agents MUST check this registry before creating new IDs. If the needed ID exists, use it exactly. If it does not exist, propose an addition - do not invent on the fly.

naming_rules.general: ALL_CAPS_WITH_UNDERSCORES. Prefix identifies the type. ID must be unique across the entire system.
naming_rules.ITM_: Paintable item. Identifies the PHYSICAL THING being painted. NEVER include phase suffixes (_PRIME, _FINISH) unless the spec family is phase-split AND a collision would occur.
naming_rules.TSK_: Task. Identifies an ACTION performed. Prefix with spec context (e.g., TSK_FRAME_, TSK_DOOR_, TSK_CEIL_) to avoid collisions across specs.
naming_rules.MOD_: SOP Module. Groups tasks into a phase. Prefix with spec context.
naming_rules.SYS_: Material System. A product combination (primer + finish). Tied to quality tiers.
naming_rules.COV_: Coverage Profile. Coverage rates for a material on a surface type.
naming_rules.CON_: Consumable. An expendable item used during work.
naming_rules.VAR_: Variant. A conditional combination of items, methods, and tiers.
naming_rules.IN_: Input. A value sourced from PaintScope. Pattern: IN_{UOM}_{WHAT}
naming_rules.PS_: PaintScope Key. External data source key. Pattern: PS_{CATEGORY}.{SURFACE_OR_ZONE}
naming_rules.SF_: Spec Family. The top-level scope identifier.
naming_rules.ROUND_: Round Configuration. A coat sequence pattern.
naming_rules.COUPLE_: Coupling Constraint. Links two tasks that must run together.
naming_rules.EXCL_: Exclusion Rule. Declares what is explicitly out of scope.
naming_rules.PRIMER_: Specialty Primer. A conditional primer product (knot sealer, etc).
naming_rules.RC_: Research Correction. A corrected finding from research phase.
naming_rules.ISS_: QA Issue. A validation problem found during QA.
naming_rules.XSPEC_: Cross-Spec Flag. A flag passed between specs to avoid double-counting.

SF_.naming_convention: SF_{SURFACE}_{CONTEXT}_{PHASE} where PHASE is optional. Use _PRIME/_FINISH suffix ONLY when prime and finish are genuinely separate spec families (different crews, different sequencing, different bid items). If the spec covers prep through finish in one scope, omit the phase suffix.

ITM_.description: Paintable Item IDs. Identifies the PHYSICAL THING being painted. The item is the constant - tasks are what you do to it.
ITM_.critical_rule: An ITM_ ID represents a physical object, NOT a phase of work. Do NOT create ITM_TRIM_CASING_DOOR_FINISH - the item is ITM_TRIM_CASING_DOOR regardless of whether you are priming or finishing it. The spec family context (SF_..._PRIME vs SF_..._FINISH) already provides the phase.
ITM_.phase_suffix_exception: ONLY use _PRIME or _FINISH suffix on an ITM_ when: (1) the prime and finish specs are separate spec families, AND (2) the same item_id would collide across those families. Even then, prefer no suffix if there is no actual collision risk.

surface_ids.description: Surface vocabulary IDs used in adjacency_declarations. These are NOT prefixed - they use lowercase_with_underscores. Canonical source: Surface_Vocabulary_Reference.md
surface_ids.rule: Always check Surface_Vocabulary_Reference.md before creating a new surface ID. The full vocabulary includes 40+ surfaces across walls, ceilings, trim, doors, windows, cabinets, built-ins, and millwork.

zone_ids.description: Protection zone IDs used in protection_zones_required and protection_metadata. Lowercase_with_underscores. Canonical source: Protection_Zones_Reference.md
zone_ids.rule: Always check Protection_Zones_Reference.md before creating a new zone ID. The full catalog includes 28 zones. Note: door_hardware appears in SF_DOOR_SLAB_INT_NC_v1 but should be migrated to hardware_covers per Protection_Zones_Reference v2.0.

PS_.description: PaintScope keys. External data source references. Pattern: PS_{CATEGORY}.{SURFACE_OR_ZONE}

Square footage of a paintable surface

IN_.description: Input IDs. Values sourced from PaintScope into spec calculations. Pattern: IN_{UOM}_{WHAT}

known_duplicates.issue: IN_EA_ROOMS vs IN_EA_ROOMS_TOTAL and IN_SF_FLOOR_AREA vs IN_SF_FLOOR_PROTECT vs IN_SF_PROTECT_FLOOR_EXPOSED all potentially reference the same data
known_duplicates.resolution: Pending consolidation. New specs should use the most specific name available.

TSK_.description: Task IDs. Each represents a discrete action performed on a paintable item. Too numerous to list individually here - see individual spec sop_modules.json files for full task lists.
TSK_.inconsistency_notes: The closet shelf spec uses short generic names (TSK_LIGHT_SAND) while other specs use context-prefixed names (TSK_FRAME_LIGHT_SAND, TSK_DOOR_LIGHT_SAND). Ceiling finish spec uses long descriptive names (TSK_LIGHT_SAND_BETWEEN_COATS_SPRAY). Future specs should use the context-prefixed pattern: TSK_{CONTEXT}_{ACTION}.

MOD_.description: SOP Module IDs. Groups tasks into a phase within a spec.
MOD_.naming_convention: MOD_{CONTEXT}_{PHASE_OR_FUNCTION}. Context should match the spec's shorthand.

VAR_.description: Variant IDs. Conditional combinations of items, methods, and tiers.
VAR_.naming_convention: VAR_{METHOD}_{CONDITION}_{TIER} or VAR_{TYPE}_{TIER}. Should be self-documenting.
VAR_.note: Variants are spec-specific and do not cross-reference. No registry needed beyond naming convention.

ROUND_.description: Round Configuration IDs. Define coat sequence patterns.

COV_.description: Coverage Profile IDs. Material coverage rates by surface condition.
COV_.notes: Only door frame spec currently uses formal coverage profile IDs. Other specs embed coverage rates directly in material_systems. Future standardization should extract all coverage data into COV_ profiles.

CON_.description: Consumable IDs. Expendable items used during work.
CON_.known_inconsistency: Closet shelf spec uses CONS_ prefix (CONS_BRUSH_ANGLE, CONS_ROLLER_MINI). Door frame spec uses CON_ prefix (CON_SANDPAPER_180, CON_BRUSH_ANGLED_SASH). The canonical prefix is CON_. CONS_ entries should be migrated.

XSPEC_.description: Cross-Spec Flags. Passed between specs to coordinate work and avoid double-counting.

XSPEC_WALL_REPAIR_DONE.description: Set by SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_PRIME when substrate inspection/repair is performed. SF_DRYWALL_WALL_NC_FINISH should skip its first inspection/repair round when this flag is set.

COMP_.description: Composition/Complexity Modifiers. Cross-spec impact when work areas overlap.

COMP_CLOSET_SHELVING.description: Closet shelving presence causes 1.5x modifier on wall/ceiling specs in same closet
